verdict.reason: The design doc specifies `durable` as a three-term conjunction and lists "IndexedDB unavailable", "Quota exhausted after eviction" and "Store writes failing" as rows that must yield durable:false (offline-local-persistence.md:326, 335-343, Goals 52-53, risk row 418). In the tree, `durable` is produced only by the app-lock election (use-durable-document.ts:182) and by `!lost`, where `lost` is latched solely from the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-108, 160-163). WafflebaseDocStore exposes no failure callback (options at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:104-138) and `withQuotaRetry` only rethrows (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:990-1016); nothing in the provider, context, chip, or offline-runtime consumes those rejections, and no IndexedDB availability probe exists outside the store. I searched repo-wide under alternative names (storeHealth/onStoreFailure/markUndurable/reportUndurable/Proxy/unhealthy/indexedDB) and found no counterexample. The repo's own plan confirms the gap as a known, unclosed limitation (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:129-134, and open item 3.4 for the per-reason tooltip), and the design doc was not amended to record it. Mitigation worth noting for triage: the durable path is currently dark behind supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67 vs pin 0.7.22 in packages/frontend/package.json:65), so no user sees `saved-locally` today — but the same task doc says the dependency bump is "the whole switch", so the over-promise ships with a one-line bump. Not refutable: the thing said to be missing really is absent.

finding.evidence: offline-local-persistence.md § Turning it on: "Two entry points, because the Settings page is not where someone is standing when they need this: **Settings** — a switch... **The sync chip** — which already reports durability, so it is the natural place to offer acquiring it"; the durability table's first row is "Offer to turn it on — this is the one row that is a call to action rather than a fault"; and the rollout table gives PR 4 as "the Settings + chip opt-in". The chip only maps states to labels/tooltips (LABELS/ICONS/tooltipFor) and never reads or writes `offline-persistence-preference`; `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is imported only by `app/settings/page.tsx` and `use-durable-document.ts`. A user stranded on `Not saved` has no way to acquire durability where they feel the need, which is the stated reason the second entry point exists.
searchedFor: grep 'turn it on'/'this device' in components/sync-status

verdict.reason: The second opt-in entry point specified by the design is genuinely absent. `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` has exactly one production caller in the entire repo — the Settings switch at app/settings/page.tsx:114 — every other reference is a test. The chip (sync-status-chip.tsx) only maps SyncState to labels/icons/tooltips; its `not-saved` tooltip (line 88) and its warning toast (line 168) are pure fault reports with no action, and the durability context it reads (lib/durable-document-context.ts:20-33) exposes no enable callback or lapse reason. Both chip mount sites (site-header.tsx:108, shared-header-status.tsx:26) render it bare. I also swept for the feature under other names (toast `action:` buttons — only offline-copy recovery in offline-runtime.tsx:135/158; text like "Turn on"/"Enable offline"/"Save on this device"; files matching *opt*/*durab*/*offline*) and found nothing. The design requires it explicitly (offline-local-persistence.md:140-147 "Two entry points… The sync chip"; :333 "Offer to turn it on — this is the one row that is a call to action"; :387 PR 4 = "the Settings + chip opt-in"; :417 the off-by-default risk is accepted *because* the chip offers the toggle). The repo's own plan corroborates the gap: 20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:91-94 leaves the tooltip-reason item 3.4 unchecked, and its wiring table lists only the Settings switch. This is an unmet acceptance item whose cost lands on the user — someone stranded on `Not saved` has no way to acquire durability where they feel the need, which is the stated reason the second entry point exists — so it is major under the design-fit rubric, not a tidiness point.

finding.summary: `durable` is never supplied to `deriveSyncState`, so the new `saved-locally` chip state is unreachable
finding.evidence: `sync-state.ts` gains a `durable?` signal and `sync-status-chip.tsx` gains a label, icon and tooltip for `saved-locally`, but `useSyncStatus` — the only caller of `deriveSyncState` in the app — still calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable`, which defaults to `false`. The design doc states the provider computes `durable` and supplies it through context, and that the fourth row dropping from destructive to muted 'is the entire user-facing value of this feature' (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees). As shipped a document can be durable while the chip still says 'Not saved' and the tooltip still tells the user their edits 'exist only in this tab' — a false statement about a persisted document, and a violation of the doc's `durable ⇒ reportable` invariant.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `durable` is never supplied to `deriveSyncState`, making the `saved-locally` chip state unreachable. The cited file contradicts this directly. use-sync-status.ts:3 imports `useDocumentDurability` from `@/lib/durable-document-context`; line 75 reads `const durable = useDocumentDurability();` with a comment saying it is published by the durable client; and line 220 calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed, durable })` — the exact fourth argument the reviewer says is absent. The quoted three-arg call appears nowhere in src (only in unit tests exercising the legacy rows). The supply chain is complete: durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:107 computes `{ store, durable: !lost, reportLoss }` and renders it through `<DurableDocumentScope value={value}>` at line 121; durable-document-context.ts:67-69 exposes it via `useDocumentDurability()`, defaulting to false only outside a durable client; sync-state.ts:85 then returns `durable ? 'saved-locally' : 'not-saved'`. This matches the design doc's stated shape (provider computes `durable`, supplies through context) and preserves the `durable => reportable` invariant via the latched `lost` flag (lines 99-105), which only ever under-reports durability. The fourth row does drop from destructive to muted for a durable document, so no acceptance criterion is unmet.

finding.summary: No opt-in control ships anywhere: neither the Settings switch nor the chip entry point, so the feature cannot be turned on
finding.evidence: The design specifies two entry points — a Settings switch beside Appearance/Dates, and an offer from the sync chip (§ Turning it on) — and the rollout table puts 'the Settings + chip opt-in' in the same PR as wiring the store. `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` is called only from its own tests; grep for 'offline' in packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx returns nothing. The store, election and durable provider are wired into `CollabDocumentProvider`, but no user can reach any of it — the stated outcome ('edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it') is unattainable.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no opt-in control ships anywhere and that the feature therefore cannot be turned on. A direct counterexample exists in the exact file the finding names. packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx:98-117 renders an "Offline" section — placed directly after the "Appearance" (line 44) and "Dates" (line 63) sections, matching the design's "Settings switch beside Appearance/Dates" — containing <Switch id="offline-switch" checked={offlineEnabled} onCheckedChange={setOfflinePersistenceEnabled} />, with per-device copy explaining that turning it off deletes stored data. The imports are at lines 20-23 and the read hook at line 31. The control is reachable by users: App.tsx:27 lazy-loads the page and App.tsx:160 routes it at /settings, with a nav entry at use-workspace-nav-items.ts:47. It also genuinely drives the wiring the finding concedes is present: use-durable-document.ts:15,109 gates on the same useOfflinePersistenceEnabled() preference the switch writes. The reviewer's two specific evidentiary claims are both false as stated: setOfflinePersistenceEnabled is not called only from tests (settings/page.tsx:114 is production code), and grepping "offline" in settings/page.tsx does not return nothing (matches on lines 21-23, 31, 93, 99, 102, 106, 112-113). Since the stated cost was that the outcome is "unattainable", the shipped and routed Settings opt-in defeats the finding regardless of the separate sync-chip offer.

searchedFor: grep offline-erase across packages/frontend/src excluding tests
finding.summary: `watchForOfflineDisable` is never started, so the toggle's central promise — 'turning this off deletes them' — is unkept
finding.evidence: `offline-erase.ts` exists with its own suite, but grep shows no importer outside `offline-erase.test.ts`. The design states 'Turning it off erases. Disabling drops every stored entry for that user on that device, including archived envelopes. A toggle that left the content behind would not be the control it presents itself as' (§ Turning it on). With no call site, disabling the preference merely stops new writes and leaves every previously stored document — full compressed content — on the device's disk until the 30-day sweep, which is itself unwired (see the cleanup finding).

verdict.reason: `watchForOfflineDisable` is started in production code. `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:12-15` imports it from `@/lib/offline-erase` and line 56-59 installs it in the mount effect (`watchForOfflineDisable(() => store, () => userId)`), tearing it down via `stopWatching()` at line 88. `OfflineRuntime` is itself mounted for every authenticated session by `packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:7,35`. The watcher body at `offline-erase.ts:135-163` subscribes to the preference, detects the enabled→disabled edge, and calls `eraseOfflineData(current, who)`, with a fallback store at line 153 for the case where Settings is the mounted route and no editor store exists — so disabling the preference does delete stored entries, exactly the design promise the finding says is unkept. Sibling wirings also exist (`api/auth.ts:4` eraseOfflineDataOnLogout, `api/documents.ts:6` purgeOfflineDocuments), and `docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:235` names `OfflineRuntime`/`PrivateRoute` as the intended host. The claim that no importer exists outside the test file is factually wrong.

finding.summary: The offline-copy recovery path has no caller, so archived unreconcilable work is never returned to the user
finding.evidence: Goal: 'Work that genuinely cannot be reconciled with the server is returned to the user as a document, not a console log', and § Losing work anyway specifies the user is told what happened with a link to the copy. `recoverOfflineCopy` and `listRecoverableWork` are imported only by their own tests. The store dutifully archives on a latched loss, but nothing lists or rehydrates archives in the app, so the archived bytes sit in IndexedDB until the (also unwired) 30-day collection deletes them — the goal is unmet and the archive is currently pure cost.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that recoverOfflineCopy/listRecoverableWork are imported only by their own tests, and that nothing lists or rehydrates archives in the app — is false. packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:7-11 imports listRecoverableWork, recoverOfflineCopy and describeArchivedDocument in production (non-test) code. The mount effect calls offerRecoverableWork (offline-runtime.tsx:80), which calls listRecoverableWork(store) (:111) and recoverOfflineCopy(store, item, ...) (:138). Lines 131-174 implement the design's "Losing work anyway" requirement literally: a persistent toast telling the user their edits could not be reconciled and are still on this device, a "Save a copy" action that rehydrates the archive into a real document, and a success toast whose "Open" action navigates to the recovered copy — i.e. the work is returned to the user as a document with a link, not a console log. The component is genuinely reachable: PrivateRoute.tsx:7 imports it and :35 renders OfflineRuntime with the signed-in user id inside the authenticated branch, so it runs once per session. The secondary claim that the 30-day collection is "also unwired" is refuted by offline-runtime.tsx:69 calling await store.collectStale(). The only nuance is that recovery is offered rather than performed automatically, which offline-runtime.tsx:97-105 documents as a deliberate choice (a declined offer is re-made next session rather than discarded) and which still satisfies the stated outcome.

finding.summary: None of the documented cleanup triggers (logout, document deleted/access lost, 30-day sweep) are wired to the store
finding.evidence: The doc's cleanup table (§ Storage) lists Logout → drop every entry for that user; document deleted or workspace access lost → drop that entry; Periodic → drop entries untouched for 30 days. `dropAllForUser`, `purge` and `collectStale` are implemented and tested, but grep finds no non-test caller anywhere in `packages/frontend/src` (nav-user.tsx's logout does not touch the store). Stored document content therefore outlives sign-out on a shared machine — the exact scenario the whole opt-in design is built around — and nothing ever reclaims quota.

verdict.reason: The claim that no non-test caller wires the store's cleanup triggers is false; all three documented triggers have production callers. (1) Logout: api/auth.ts:4,105 — logout() awaits eraseOfflineDataOnLogout(), which in lib/offline-erase.ts:65-79 constructs a WafflebaseDocStore for the remembered user and calls eraseOfflineData → store.dropAllForUser (offline-erase.ts:30); the identity is supplied by rememberOfflineUser(userId) in components/offline-runtime.tsx:42. nav-user.tsx not touching the store is immaterial because it invokes api/auth.ts's logout(). (2) Document deleted: api/documents.ts:6,167,215 call purgeOfflineDocuments, which calls store.purgeDocument per id (offline-erase.ts:92-109). (3) Thirty-day sweep: components/offline-runtime.tsx:69 awaits store.collectStale() once per session, and OfflineRuntime is mounted in production at PrivateRoute.tsx:35. Additionally the toggle-off erase is wired via watchForOfflineDisable (offline-runtime.tsx:56-59 → offline-erase.ts:120-165). Therefore stored content does not outlive sign-out and quota is reclaimed by the session sweep.
